description.narrative:
Mozambique continues to experience the impacts of sustained heavy rainfall and widespread flooding as of 18 January 2026, with cumulative precipitation across southern and central regions maintaining elevated _flood risk in the Maputo, Incomáti, Limpopo,Save, Búzi, Púngoè, Inharrime and Zambeze river basins. Hydrometric stations remain at or near alert thresholds and continued rainfall is expected to further increase runoff and trigger flooding. As of 17 January 2026, national data from the Government of Mozambique’s National Institute for Disaster Management (INGD) indicates that approximately 432,000 people have been affected by heavy rains across the provinces of Maputo, Gaza, Inhambane, Sofala and Zambézia, with Gaza being the most affected province(330,000 people). The latestupdate from INGD, on January 18, indicates a significant increase in the number of people affected, from 432,000 to 645,781 people (112,863 HH). Oxfam and its partner, with the support of CAT Fund, will initially focus theirefforts on needs assessment activities and and kickstart response, particularly in Water and Hygiene interventions in the Southern region of Mozambique, specifically in Gaza province. Oxfam will also work to strengthen the capacity of local communities and its partners to respond to future humanitarianemergencies. Below are the main activities that Oxfam intends to implement in this initial phase of the crisis response:
Project Target: 2,500 people (550 Females, 450 Males and 1,500 Children).
Key Activities: 1. Participate in coordination meetings and monitoring missions. 2. Data collection and needs assessment. 3. Coordinate Oxfam's network of local partners for effective engagement in needs assessments. 4. Produce SitReps and share with stakeholders. 5. Document the impacts of floods through MEDIA. 6. Develop concept notes and response proposals. 7. Water and hygiene kit distribution for the most vulnerable families living in accommodation centers/communities (during needs assessment the team will identify the target community and beneficiaries).
Monitoring and Accountability
Oxfam’s MEAL department will support the monitoring and quality function of the response.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
